newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade union body says Bundesbank "foolish".
newsitem.headline: German trade union body says Bundesbank "foolish".

text.p: Germany's DGB federation of trade unions said on Thursday the Bundesbank's views on Germany's still-shaky economy was "foolish" and urged the central bank to spur growth by cutting interest rates.

DGB board member Michael Geuenich told a news briefing that the Bundesbank should use the current low-inflation outlook to "give a breath of fresh air" both to domestic investment and also consumer demand by lowering key interest rates.

Geuenich said the central bank's advice to the government to cut public spending in order to reduce government deficits would make the sluggish economy, and Germany's chronic unemployment problem, even worse.
The Bundesbank, in a move widely expected, earlier on Thursday left key interest rates unchanged.

Many of Bundesbankers, including president Hans Tietmeyer, have said a further rate cut would not by itself create more jobs, agreeing with Bonn that a wide reform of the labour market was urgently needed.
